question: What concession is being made about form such that even under that concession no impossibility arises for the claim at stake?
premises: A concessive force attaches to the case of possessing form.
Negation is applied to the existence of any impossibility.
The subject of that negation is impossibility itself.
inference: Even if form is present, no impossibility arises in the case under consideration.
uncertainties: The exact referent of the concession remains dependent on prior context.
plain_english: Even in the case of form, there is no impossibility.
